fb_tap_position: Tap a position on the pitch
fb_tip_mentality: More attacking = more shots and goals, but more space behind your defence.
fb_tip_passing: Short keeps the ball and is safer; direct reaches the box faster with more risk.
fb_tip_tempo: Fast tempo creates chances quicker but causes more errors and fatigue.
fb_tip_width: Wide play brings more crosses; narrow play crowds the middle.
fb_tip_focus: Middle = through balls (vision, passing); flanks = crosses (crossing, heading).
fb_tip_pressing: High pressing wins the ball higher up but tires your players.
fb_tip_defline: A high line squeezes the midfield but is open to balls in behind.
fb_tip_marking: Man-marking shuts down strikers; clever movers can escape it.
fb_tip_counter: Break quickly after winning the ball in your own half.
fb_tip_offside: Catches runners more often; needs well-drilled defenders.
fb_tip_time_wasting: When leading after the hour mark the team slows the game down.
fb_tip_hard_tackling: Wins more duels, but brings more fouls, cards and penalties.
fb_tip_training_focus: The chosen area's attributes improve about 50% faster for the whole squad.
fb_tip_intensity: Light: slower development, fewer injuries, fresher legs. Intense: +15% development, almost twice the training injuries, lower match fitness.
fb_tip_coaches: Better coaches and facilities speed up development. Hire coaches in the Club section.
fb_gb_basics:
You are the boss of the club: you pick the team and tactics, sign and sell players, set training, build facilities and manage the money.

Press Continue to move through the calendar. The game stops on your match days and when something needs your attention (offers, contract news, youth intake).

On match day you can play the match or get a quick result. Everything is saved automatically.
fb_gb_mentality:
Mentality sets how many risks your team takes.

• Very defensive / defensive: fewer players join attacks, fewer shots for both sides. Good when protecting a lead or facing a much stronger team.
• Balanced: the default.
• Attacking / very attacking: more shots and goals, but the opponent finds more space. In our tests a strong side scored about 18% more but also conceded more.

Combine defensive mentality with counter-attack to punish opponents who push forward.
fb_gb_passing:
• Short: many safe passes, high possession (about 60%+), fewer but cleaner attacks. Needs good passing and first touch.
• Mixed: balanced.
• Direct: long balls towards the forwards. Possession drops to around 40%, the ball reaches the box faster, games become more open. Works with tall, strong strikers and good long passers.
fb_gb_tempo:
Fast tempo moves the ball quickly: more chances and shots, but more misplaced passes and more fatigue.

Slow tempo keeps the ball and controls the game; it suits short passing and protecting a lead.
fb_gb_width:
Wide: your wide players stay out on the touchline, which creates more crosses. Needs good crossers and strong headers in the box.

Narrow: the team plays through the middle and stays compact; good with a playmaker and through balls.
fb_gb_focus:
Through the middle: more through balls. Success depends on your passers' vision and passing against the defenders' marking, and on your forwards' pace. A one-on-one is the best chance in football.

Down the flanks: more crosses. A cross becomes a header chance if your target man beats the centre-back in the air.
fb_gb_pressing:
High pressing hunts the ball in the opponent's half. It works best against players with low composure and wins the ball close to goal, but players lose condition faster during the match.

Low pressing saves energy and keeps the shape; the opponent has time on the ball in its own half.
fb_gb_defline:
High line: defenders step up, the midfield becomes narrow and hard to pass through. But balls over the top and through balls against pacey forwards become dangerous – in tests a high line conceded more than twice as many goals against fast strikers.

Deep line: the box is protected, through balls rarely work, but the opponent controls the game. Ideal with counter-attack.
fb_gb_marking:
Zonal: every player guards an area. Safe default.

Man-to-man: your defenders follow their direct opponent. Great if your defenders mark well; but forwards with excellent off-the-ball movement can still escape.
fb_gb_counter:
When the ball is won in your own half the team breaks quickly with fewer passes and more through balls.

It is deadly against opponents who attack with many players or play a high line (in tests: over 3 goals per game against a very attacking side). The price: fewer players join normal attacks.
fb_gb_offside: Your defence steps up together to catch attackers offside. Defenders with good teamwork make it work much more often. When it fails the attacker is through on goal.
fb_gb_time_wasting: When you are ahead after the 60th minute your players slow everything down: more backward passes, longer breaks. The referee may show yellow cards for it.
fb_gb_hard_tackling: Tackles become harder: your players win more duels, but commit more fouls, collect more cards and cause more penalties. Opponents get injured more often.
fb_gb_formations:
Choose a formation that suits your best players. Tap a position on the pitch, then a player from the list to put him there (players already in the XI swap places).

The number under each player is his rating in that position; a red ring means he is not familiar with it. Players can learn new positions in training.

Auto pick lets the assistant choose; Best formation picks the shape with the highest total rating. Injured and banned players are replaced automatically.
fb_gb_training:
Players grow toward their potential every week. The speed depends on:
• Age: fastest between 16 and 21, slows after 24, stops around 29.
• Gap between current ability and potential.
• Coaches and training facilities (youth coach and youth facilities for under-19s).
• Personality: professionalism and determination.
• Playing time (very important under 23) and morale.
• Intensity: light, normal or intense.

Team focus speeds up one area for everyone; individual focus speeds up an area a lot for one player. After 30 (goalkeepers 32) players decline, physical attributes first, while decisions and positioning can still improve.
fb_gb_coaches:
• Coaches: each training area uses the coach attribute for it (attack, defence, technique, tactics, mental, fitness, goalkeeping). Around five coaches cover all areas; with fewer, quality drops.
• Youth coach: develops under-19s and improves the yearly youth intake.
• Physio: shortens injuries and reduces training injuries.
• Fitness coach: slows the decline of older players.
• Assistant: man management lifts morale; judges your own players' potential.
• Scouts: the better they are, the more accurate the ability and potential estimates of other clubs' players.
fb_gb_morale:
Morale changes every week. It goes up with good results, enough playing time for the player's status (key players expect to start most games), a fair wage, good social facilities and a good assistant. Very unhappy ambitious players ask to leave.

Form is the average of recent match ratings. Both morale and form slightly change a player's strength on match day and his development.
fb_gb_youth:
Every year on 15 March 2–8 youngsters (15–16 years old) join your academy. Youth recruitment decides how many and how good, youth facilities and the youth coach add quality, and your country's football level matters too. Now and then a golden talent appears.

Give young players minutes and good coaching: development is fastest before 21.
fb_gb_finance:
Income: tickets (home matches; a higher ticket price earns more per fan but fills fewer seats), TV money (half shared equally, half by league position), merchandise (grows with reputation and star players), shirt sponsor, stadium advertising, prize money (cups and especially European competitions) and player sales.

Expenses: player and staff wages, facility upkeep, youth academy, matchday costs, transfers and building work. A negative balance costs 0.12% interest per week.

Investor bonus: watch a video to add money to the club, 3 times a week.

Bank (Club › Bank): take one loan at a time for 1–3 years. The credit limit grows with your income and reputation; clubs with a high reputation pay less interest, and it is higher while your balance is negative. The instalment is paid every Monday and paying off early costs 1% extra. A savings deposit earns 2% a year, but money in it can't be spent until you withdraw it. The Finances page shows this month's and last month's total income and expenses.
fb_gb_transfers:
Windows: 1 July – 1 September and January. Free agents can be signed at any time.

The selling club's price depends on how important the player is for them, his age and potential, his contract length (cheap in the last year), whether he is listed, and the seller's finances. A release clause cannot be refused.

After the fee is agreed, negotiate wage and years with the player – too low and he walks away after three tries. Loans: you pay a share of the wage and the player returns at the end of the season.

You can list your own players, offer them for loan or start a 3-day auction where clubs outbid each other. Shortlist players you like and watch the rumours.
fb_gb_contracts:
Renew the contracts of important players in time. On 1 January you are warned about contracts that end this season; from mid-January other clubs can sign them on a pre-contract and they leave for free in the summer.

Players ask for a raise when they improve. Releasing a player costs 60% of his remaining wages.
fb_gb_competitions:
Every European country has its leagues with promotion and relegation (some second tiers have play-offs), a national cup and a super cup.

European places depend on your league position and the country ranking, which changes every season with European results: Champions Cup, Europa Cup and Conference Cup each have qualifying rounds, a 36-team league phase and knockout rounds.

National teams play the Nations League, qualifiers, the European Championship and the World Cup.
fb_gb_hidden:
Ability and potential are shown as stars estimated by your staff, so they can be wrong – especially with weak scouts.

Watch a short video on a player's card to reveal his exact current ability, his exact potential and his hidden personality: consistency, big-match temperament, injury proneness, professionalism, ambition, loyalty, adaptability, pressure handling and versatility. The player stays revealed for good (green stars).
